title: Hilary Duff ate New England clam chowder and a Dunkin’ Munchkin on stage during her Mass. concert
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Hilary Duff tried New England clam chowder and a Dunkin' Munchkin on stage during her Mansfield concert.
Duff expressed her initial reluctance to try clam chowder but was pleasantly surprised by its taste.
Her food-tasting events are part of her 'The Lucky Me Tour,' including regional dishes at various concert stops.

title: Adley Rutschman ready to make his debut with Red Sox on Tuesday
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman, acquired by the Red Sox from the Orioles on August 3, is set to debut against the Blue Jays.
Rutschman plans to ease into his role, having played two rehab games with Triple-A Worcester last weekend.
The Red Sox may need to adjust their roster, possibly by optioning Connor Wong or designating Jake Rogers for assignment.

title: Springfield zoo suffers devastating damage during severe storm
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Severe storm uprooted trees and destroyed enclosures at The Zoo in Forest Park, Springfield; no animals were injured.
The Zoo in Forest Park will remain closed indefinitely as staff assess storm damage, impacting financial stability.
Springfield declared a state of emergency due to storm, with power outages and 45 people displaced from a collapsed building.

title: 2 dead in crash on Marlborough highway
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Two people died in a multi-car crash on I-290 East in Marlborough, Massachusetts, on Monday afternoon.
The Solomon Pond Road exit on I-290 East near I-495 was closed to traffic following the incident.
Authorities advise drivers to use alternate routes due to expected significant delays and heavy traffic.

title: Body recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A body was recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury after a reported drowning on Sunday.
Police and dive teams used sonar and drones in a search that ended with the body being found early Monday.
The victim's identity has not been released, and the investigation into the drowning incident is ongoing.

title: Undrafted Patriots linebacker is carving out a roster spot
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Khalil Jacobs, undrafted from University of Missouri, is standing out in New England Patriots training camp.
Jacobs, known for his play speed, was signed despite an unimpressive 4.77 40-yard dash time.
Jacobs showed promise in intra-squad scrimmages, contributing to defensive plays against starting quarterbacks.

title: Gov. Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights — here’s what to know
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights, removing Massachusetts' gestational limits on abortions after 24 weeks.
The law lets physicians perform abortions based on their professional judgment, reducing requirements for a medical-review process.
Supporters argue it reduces travel for abortion care; opponents claim it weakens protections for unborn children and oversight.

title: Lost gravestone of free Black man who died in 1729 uncovered in downtown Boston
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: The gravestone of Sebastian, a free Black man who died in 1729, was uncovered at Boston's Granary Burying Ground.
Sebastian, also known as Boston, transitioned from being enslaved to free and advocated for marriage rights.
The gravestone, considered the oldest for a free Black person in the U.S., was restored and reset at its original location.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Carlton Davis and Will Campbell returned to Patriots practice, while Charles Woods and Christian Barmore remained absent.
Receiver Romeo Doubs made a highlight-reel catch during practice, showcasing offensive potential alongside Kyle Williams.
Patriots prepare for joint practice with Colts as the team continues to focus on improvement and competition.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A Scarborough Beach lifeguard was pulled underwater by a white shark while using a rescue torpedo, officials reported.
The lifeguard freed himself, swam to shore, and the beach was temporarily closed for safety assessment thereafter.
Scarborough officials warned of continued white shark activity, advising caution and reporting sightings to lifeguards.
